PRAXIS_UI_LAB.TITLE: Praxis UI Lab
PRAXIS_UI_LAB.DESCRIPTION: A day list for a medical practice: appointments move by click or keyboard from "planned" to "completed", and waiting times and warnings are visible at a glance. An independent case study with synthetic patient data.
PRAXIS_UI_LAB.IMPLEMENTATION: Angular 22 without Zone.js, built with standalone components, signals and strict TypeScript. The domain logic lives in its own framework-free layer: a state machine for appointments, derived waiting times with thresholds and a Europe/Berlin time facade. Six signal stores hold the state. Every API call follows an OpenAPI contract and is answered by Mock Service Worker from fixed test data. The UI reports conflicting edits (409) and stale data (412) separately. The day list works fully by keyboard and command palette, statuses show as icon, text and colour, and there are three density modes. Unit tests run in GitLab CI, and Playwright checks the flows and accessibility with axe.

STADTPULS.TITLE: StadtPuls
STADTPULS.TECH: Node.js | Moleculer | Vue 3 | PostgreSQL | InfluxDB | Keycloak
STADTPULS.DESCRIPTION: An IoT platform for municipal utilities: LoRaWAN readings from water meters and sensors arrive validated in a dashboard with a site tree, a map and consumption charts. Each tenant sees only its own assets.
STADTPULS.IMPLEMENTATION: Node.js services built with Moleculer and connected over RabbitMQ. Incoming uplinks are validated, deduplicated and decoded in a sandboxed driver runtime. Measurement time and ingest time stay separate, so no misleading time series appear. Master data lives in PostgreSQL, measurements in InfluxDB 2. The REST API is generated as OpenAPI from the route table and uses keyset pagination. Keycloak issues OIDC tokens, and permissions plus scopes keep tenants apart. The Vue 3 dashboard is bilingual and signs in with PKCE. 253 automated tests, 9 browser tests against the production bundle and a 15-job GitLab pipeline back it up.

VIDEOFLIX.TITLE: Videoflix
VIDEOFLIX.TECH: Python | Django REST | Redis | FFmpeg | Docker
VIDEOFLIX.DESCRIPTION: A Netflix-style video streaming platform. Register, sign in and watch videos as HLS streams in three quality levels (480p/720p/1080p). Uploaded videos are transcoded automatically in the background.
VIDEOFLIX.IMPLEMENTATION: Complete Django REST backend: authentication with JWTs in HttpOnly cookies including email activation and password reset, video upload with FFmpeg transcoding into three resolutions via a Redis/RQ task queue, and delivery as HLS segments. Runs in production in Docker behind a reverse proxy on my own server. Backend and deployment are entirely my own work.

BOOKSTORE.TITLE: Bookstore
BOOKSTORE.DESCRIPTION: A bilingual bookstore with server-side rendering. Visitors browse a curated catalogue, pan across a Three.js wall of covers and ask for books by mood, for example "something dreamy for a rainy day".
BOOKSTORE.IMPLEMENTATION: Angular 21 with SSR and hydration, signal-based stores and strictly typed code throughout. The recommender works in three tiers: first an AI endpoint, then an embedding model running locally on the server when no key is available, and finally a keyword search. Every query gets an answer, even when the external service is unreachable. The API key stays in the backend and never reaches the browser. Accessibility is audited automatically with axe against WCAG AA, alongside unit tests, end-to-end tests and Lighthouse budgets in CI. Deployed in Docker behind a Caddy reverse proxy.

CODERR.TITLE: Coderr
CODERR.DESCRIPTION: Coderr is a service marketplace where businesses create offers and customers order and review the work.
CODERR.IMPLEMENTATION: I built the complete Django REST API. It covers role-based permissions, nested serializers, filtering, pagination and database annotations. Orders store the agreed offer conditions as an immutable snapshot. 88 automated tests cover the core API flows. The production application runs on PostgreSQL, Docker, Gunicorn and Caddy. The frontend was provided as a course template.

QUIZLY.TITLE: Quizly
QUIZLY.TECH: Python | Django REST | Whisper | Gemini | Docker
QUIZLY.DESCRIPTION: Turns any YouTube video into a multiple-choice quiz: submit a URL, and the AI pipeline transcribes the audio with Whisper and generates a ten-question quiz with Google Gemini.
QUIZLY.IMPLEMENTATION: Django REST backend with a complete AI pipeline: audio download, Whisper transcription and Gemini quiz generation. Authentication uses JWTs in HttpOnly cookies with refresh token rotation and blacklisting. The static frontend was provided as a course template. Backend, AI integration and Docker deployment are my own work.

JOIN.TITLE: Join
JOIN.DESCRIPTION: Task manager inspired by the Kanban System. Create and organize tasks using drag and drop functions, assign users and categories.
JOIN.IMPLEMENTATION: As the team's frontend developer, I designed and built the user interactions and kept the app fully responsive, owning the frontend independently at every stage.

POLLO.TITLE: El Pollo Loco
POLLO.DESCRIPTION: Jump, run and throw game based on object-oriented approach. Help Pepe to find coins and tabasco salsa to fight against the crazy hen.
POLLO.IMPLEMENTATION: Built entirely from scratch using vanilla JavaScript and object-oriented programming. Implemented game physics, collision detection, and sprite animations while managing game state and user input.

POKEDEX.TITLE: Pokédex Holo TCG
POKEDEX.DESCRIPTION: A from-scratch rebuild of a Pokédex that shows all 1025 Pokémon from the PokéAPI as holographic trading cards. Opening one reveals a mouse-tilting 3D card in TCG style. It's fully bilingual (EN/DE), with translated names, types and abilities, plus search, filters, evolution chains and a compare mode.
POKEDEX.IMPLEMENTATION: A remake of an earlier vanilla project as a modern Next.js app. The first page is server-rendered, then the client takes over search, type/generation/favorite filters and a URL-driven detail dialog. The 3D card is built with Three.js / React Three Fiber (a drawn canvas texture plus a holographic sheen). Full EN/DE localization via bundled name/ability data, plus a low-graphics mode (pixel sprites) for weaker devices and bulk loading. Shipped as a static export (no server required), with PWA/offline caching, a sitemap, and unit (Vitest) + end-to-end (Playwright) tests.

PRAXIS.NAME: Praxis UI Lab
PRAXIS.TITLE: A day list that makes workflows easy to follow.
PRAXIS.SUMMARY: A demo for a medical practice: appointments move by click or keyboard from "planned" to "completed", and waiting times and warnings are visible at a glance. All patient data is synthetic.
PRAXIS.CONTRIBUTION: Solo project. Concept, interface, domain logic and tests are mine.
PRAXIS.PROBLEM: How can a day list show the state of every appointment without losing concurrent edits or stale data?
PRAXIS.TECH: Angular 22 without Zone.js, signal stores, an OpenAPI contract, Mock Service Worker, Playwright with axe.
PRAXIS.DECISION: The domain logic lives framework-free in its own layer: a state machine for appointments and time logic for Europe/Berlin. The interface reports conflicts (409) and stale versions (412) separately.
PRAXIS.RESULT: Live demo with synthetic data. Unit tests run in GitLab CI, Playwright checks workflows and accessibility.
PRAXIS.MEDIA_LABEL: Screen recording: in the Praxis UI Lab day list a patient is selected and called in, followed by search, the command palette with compact density and the history.

STADTPULS.NAME: StadtPuls
STADTPULS.TITLE: From a reading to an application.
STADTPULS.SUMMARY: An IoT platform for municipal utilities: LoRaWAN readings from meters and sensors are validated and land in a dashboard with a site tree, a map and consumption charts. Each tenant only sees their own assets.
STADTPULS.CONTRIBUTION: Ongoing solo project. Services, API, storage, dashboard and pipeline are mine.
STADTPULS.PROBLEM: Readings arrive twice, late or broken. Time series still have to be correct and tenants cleanly separated.
STADTPULS.TECH: Node.js services with Moleculer and RabbitMQ, PostgreSQL for master data, InfluxDB 2 for readings, Keycloak (OIDC), Vue 3.
STADTPULS.DECISION: Measurement time and arrival time stay separate so no false time series appear. Incoming data is validated, de-duplicated and decoded in an isolated driver runtime.
STADTPULS.RESULT: 253 automated tests, 9 browser tests against the production bundle and a GitLab pipeline with 15 jobs. Live demo and code are public.
STADTPULS.MEDIA_LABEL: Screen recording of StadtPuls with demo data: overview with map, the Hafen site with consumption over 7 and 30 days, then the device list filtered to water meters.

ZYKLUS.NAME: Zyklus
ZYKLUS.STACK: React · PWA · offline sync · Hono API
ZYKLUS.TITLE: Training and nutrition, even offline.
ZYKLUS.SUMMARY: A mobile training app with a plan generator, set logging, a food diary and progress views. Installable, usable offline and available in three languages.
ZYKLUS.CONTRIBUTION: Personal project. I modelled the feature set on an existing training app and built it entirely myself.
ZYKLUS.PROBLEM: Gyms often have poor reception. Entries still need to be saved immediately and synced between devices later.
ZYKLUS.TECH: React PWA, custom sync layer, API with Hono and node:sqlite, Vitest and Playwright in a mobile viewport.
ZYKLUS.DECISION: Plan generator, progression and calorie targets live outside React in a tested domain layer. Sync conflicts are merged per entry.
ZYKLUS.RESULT: Runs live on my server. Using it requires an account.

CODERR.TITLE: A service marketplace as a clean API.
CODERR.SUMMARY: Businesses publish offers, customers order and review services. I built the complete Django REST backend.
CODERR.CONTRIBUTION: Backend and deployment are mine. The frontend was provided as a course template.
